We derive exact analytical solutions for two types of quasiparticle excitations on a Laughlin ground state. In the first case, two quasiparticles with opposite signs combine to form a charge-neutral holon excitation. In the second scenario, two quasiparticles with the same sign create a charge-imbalanced maxon excitation. Our analytical approach confirms a previously suggested correlation between the energy cost and correlation function of the two quasiparticle configurations. Notably, we are the first to provide precise analytical expressions for these relationships. In addition, we verify that the energy cost of creating a maxon and a holon scales similarly when the system's interaction strength and filling fraction vary.

In the context of glaciology, particularly when modeling grounding line problems, a Stokes variational inequality with semicoercive properties arises. This study focuses on the numerical approach, investigating the existence and approximation properties of a finite element solution for this semicoercive Stokes variational inequality. It is set in a 2-dimensional domain with a Lipschitz-continuous boundary and features a non-convex set of admissible Stokes problems. The work presents positive results, including the existence of finite element solutions and semicoercive sub-solutions, as well as the convergence of these sub-solutions in the weakly lower-semi-continuous Galerkin space. The study highlights the significance of the contact condition in glaciology and supersedes a previous incorrect analysis.

Galactic supergiants create powerful outflows that have a profound impact on star formation, but the details of their impact remain unclear. Using observations from KCWI, we studied a rapidly growing galaxy at a distance of 2.8 billion lightyears and found that outflows influence star formation in a localized manner. Outflows in this galaxy control star formation through outflow-driven winds that affect gas in the center of the galaxy. This effect is seen in star-forming regions near the galaxy's core, where star formation slows down in regions with high outflow rates. In contrast, regions with low outflow rates in the center continue to form stars at a high rate. In addition, we found that outflows in the center of the galaxy are triggered by star-forming regions in a delayed manner, 10 million years after the initial star explosion. This delayed response is seen in the movement of gas in the center, which is seen as a 'tail' forming behind it. This indicates that outflows in the center of the galaxy are triggered by star-forming regions, which push gas towards the outskirts of the galaxy, creating a 'tail' of gas in the process.

Our study examines the connection between the initial state geometry and anisotropic flow in medium-energy Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions using a multiphase transport model. We discovered that triangular flow is more responsive to initial states with triangular structure than those with random initial conditions. The triangular flow signal in Au+Au collisions is significantly smaller than that in Cu+Cu collisions due to the larger initial geometry in Au+Au. The larger triangular flow in Cu+Cu collisions results from a greater contribution from the third harmonic elliptical momentum, denoted p_3, in Cu+Cu. The relationship between p_3 and the transport coefficient shows that a lower density and higher velocity gradients contribute to a larger triangular flow. The interactions between particles and the distance over which they interact are key factors affecting triangular flow. The collective flow of particles in Cu+Cu collisions is more sensitive to these factors than in Au+Au collisions.

A novel method is presented to simulate robotic structure simulations in space, utilizing ABAQUS software and an updated theory of beam stiffness. Previously, researchers combined beam and shell models but failed to account for interdependent variable effects such as warping and bending. By correcting these omissions, improved simulations of robotic structures can be achieved, resulting in more accurate representations of their physical behavior. Key to this simulation is the integration of 3D Euler-Bernoulli beam models into ABAQUS, a process facilitated by the software's compatibility with user-written macros. Through practical application and theoretical validation, it is demonstrated that the simplified model offers a practical and efficient solution for structural analysis.

Recent research has shown that pre-training neural networks on large, unlabeled image datasets can significantly improve performance for various downstream tasks.  Many researchers have proposed different approaches to pre-training, but the relative effectiveness of these methods and the benefits they provide have not been well understood.  In this research, we investigate whether training on a task that estimates depth from a single image leads to better pre-training than classification for semantic segmentation.  We test this hypothesis by comparing the effectiveness of pre-training on datasets from a classification task and a depth estimation task and examine the impact on downstream tasks.  Our results show that while pre-training on a large dataset leads to some improvement, training on a depth estimation dataset leads to a substantially larger gain in performance.  We also found that the benefit of pre-training on a dataset with a different modality (i.e. depth vs. classification) is due to the fact that such a dataset is less likely to suffer from overfitting to the training set.  Finally, in an effort to make our research more accessible, we have made available the code used to test our hypotheses at  https://github.com/berndjhuwaldshahl/depth-vs-classification .

This article presents a cohesive overview of the concept of enhanced Bohr radii for families of harmonic mappings. A key finding demonstrated in [M. Nowak, J. Nonlinear Anal.: Theory, Methods and Applications 74(10)(2010): 3075-3084], showed that the class $\mathcal{L}$ does not behave well in relation to this topic. Conversely, this study finds that the class of log-harmonic mappings exhibiting starlike behavior provides a suitable framework for investigation. A specific result established in this context includes: If $f$ is a non-zero, analytic, univalent, starlike log-harmonic mapping of the unit disk $U$ into the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$, then for $p > 0$, the series $$\sum_{n=1}\frac{2p\alpha_1}{n(n+1)}z^n$$ represents an optimal coefficient estimate of $f$ in the class of log-harmonic mappings. A corresponding numerical value of $p$ is also provided in this scenario.

We present a method for estimating Kendall's tau nonparametric rank correlation coefficient, based on haplotype-specific pair-wise associations. This approach effectively accounts for linked traits resulting from single nucleotide polymorphisms. As a consequence, our method yields improved estimates of tau, especially in small samples, while maintaining its qualitative characteristics. The proposed method can be seen as a form of block-wise Brownmore's nonparametric test and is further validated by extensive simulation studies and an example real-world application.

Intelligent Edge Systems are now being used in a variety of safety-related applications for vehicular networks, thanks to the development of advanced technologies such as 5G, cloud computing, and IoT. To ensure that these systems operate within safety and regulatory frameworks, it's essential to address two significant challenges: the protection of privacy for users and the verification of trustworthiness. This requires innovative solutions that integrate multi-layered privacy protection mechanisms, localized trust verification systems, and transparent AI models. This paper will explore a comprehensive framework for privacy-protecting edge intelligence in vehicular networks, focusing on the development of privacy-enhancing techniques and the evaluation of their performance in terms of privacy protection and trust assessment. This framework will be applied to several real-world use cases, including local fusion of sensor data and edge-based detection of attacks. The results will be made available to the public, along with the source code. This paper's primary contribution is a versatile framework that can be used to evaluate and assess privacy protection mechanisms for intelligent edge systems in vehicular networks. This framework can also be applied to other areas, such as smart cities, medical applications, and social media, to name a few.

We introduce a new class of surfaces, referred to as Euler topology surfaces, with the primary characteristic being that their local vanishing points, determined by Euler's omega function, form a curve that does not have any singular points, such as aci-orientability and causticity. These properties enable the existence of specialized transition curves like Euler ramps and infinitesimal rotation transition surfaces.

The modified Holling-Tanner predator-prey model incorporates critical aspects of both models and has been widely used in ecological studies, however it neglects the Allee effect which is crucial in understanding and predicting some species' population dynamics. This paper aims to develop a new model that builds upon the Holling-Tanner framework while incorporating a strong Allee effect in the prey population, thereby ensuring the model's sustainability. By using mathematical methods, we have analyzed the stationary solutions and examined the long-term behavior of both the prey and predator populations, ultimately concluding that the system can support multiple coexisting equilibrium states.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Aspect Pivot Simplex (APS) method for linear programming. Developed from the simplex method, APS incorporates two innovative strategies: the use of balanced, equivalent basis transformations and the systematic, forward-thinking direction selection process with the aspect ratio. Building on the initial APS algorithm, this study showcases an improved, streamlined version that achieves a linear iteration threshold. Moreover, this paper provides a detailed examination of the underlying principles of the balanced, equivalent basis transformation technique in the context of the simplex method. A fundamental theorem of this study outlines the underlying principles of the iteration process for the APS algorithm. A new, streamlined version of APS is proposed in this study, featuring a method for selecting directions with the maximum aspect ratio, resulting in a method with a linear iteration threshold. A comprehensive numerical test was conducted to assess the performance of this new algorithm.

P. Bak introduced an extension of the modular group along with its associated generalization of the Shimura-Langlands conjecture. The NK_1 of Bak's modular group, analogous to the classical Nk_1, serves as an important component in exploring preimages of Hecke operators in the Hecke algebra. The paper focuses on calculating the NK_1 of Bak's modular group over graded rings with specific characteristics.

This paper delves into the distinction between on-shell and off-shell top quark Compton scattering when considering a strictly on-shell case, and expands upon this by incorporating both real and virtual off-shell contributions with non-zero transverse momentum.  These processes are examined in the context of pp -> ttj events, with an emphasis on how off-shell effects impact the measurement of the top quark mass.  Calculations in both a fixed-order framework and in Drell-Yan parton model are used to investigate this influence, with findings indicating that while off-shell contributions may not significantly alter the average top quark mass, they can result in increased statistical uncertainty in the measurement.  This outcome is attributed to the interference between on-shell and off-shell Compton scattering amplitudes, with further research necessary to determine if corrections from additional processes would mitigate this effect.

As the deep learning field continues to evolve, the popularity of transformers is growing, and they are being explored for multi-modal applications such as image and video analysis using attention-based mechanisms. A recent study demonstrated the effectiveness of vision transformers in detecting synthetic faces used in voice conversion, and we build upon this research by investigating its applicability to detecting forged videos in zero-shot scenarios. We identify key issues with the study's results and present our own findings, which are based on a more thorough examination of the same problem. Our improvements include more accurate and reliable benchmark tests and the use of more realistic datasets to validate the efficacy of zero-shot synthetic video detection. We also propose a novel approach to synthetic video synthesis using a pre-trained image transformer, which outperforms existing models and achieves state-of-the-art results on zero-shot synthetic video detection.

A significant challenge in the field of AI has been to create a functional self-driving car system. This task necessitates the development of an algorithm capable of making the system self-learnable. This report outlines the development process of a Deep Reinforcement Learning model in resolving the self-driving car challenge. Utilizing Python with the Unity engine, the model leverages PyTorch for deep learning and the multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm from stable agents. Key milestones include understanding the challenge, framework setup, simulation configuration, model implementation, and data storage. Additionally, the report covers critical concepts including state-space design, calibration of sensor equipment, model training, data visualization, and documentation.

Evolutionary algorithms have seen significant advancements in solving complex multi-objective optimization problems, particularly through parallel computing, which has proven effective in reducing overall computational time, thus speeding up data generation and enhancing solution quality. Nevertheless, the parallel computing approach introduces evaluation time bias, where the algorithm's performance is biased towards solutions evaluated quickest. This has led to the development of asynchronous parallel multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, which can minimize the impact of bias. Unfortunately, existing APMOEA solutions often overlook parent selection, which contributes to the bias, or inadequately address it. This paper presents an innovative parent selection scheme, designed to mitigate the effects of evaluation time bias in APMOEA. The proposed method involves assigning parent IDs as a function of frequency of solution involvement in non-dominated sets, rather than relying on the traditional crowded distance metric. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed approach outperforms existing solutions, showcasing improved diversity and convergence even when faced with the Max-Voronoi boundary, a problem known for its high computational difficulty.

Recent research has yielded a highly influential gravitational lensing event, OGLE-2017-BLG-1434, characterized by a long-lasting quasar-like light curve, resulting in a highly precise analysis of the lensing system. Our analysis using the Keck Observatory's adaptive optics reveals a cold super-Earth with a mass similar to that of Earth and an extremely low surface temperature. The planet's mass and temperature were confirmed through verification and are consistent with previous predictions. Notably, this detection contributes significantly to our understanding of low-mass planet formation, particularly in systems with minimal angular momentum.

The concept of time-oscillating open quantum systems is expanded upon, with a focus on enhancing the system evolution rate, similar to the approach in closed quantum systems. An approximation method for the master equation is developed, which at second order maintains analytically the Markov nature of the system evolution. The primary outcome is a set of modified Hamiltonians that account for non-Markov behavior and a set of ordinary differential equations that describe the post-collision behavior. Interestingly, when the oscillation frequency is high enough, the behavior can be accurately represented by modified Hamiltonians that are effectively time-averaged. The method has clear applications in quantum optics but can also be applied more broadly to any system where a perturbative approach can be applied.

Recent studies of CePd$_{1-x}$Rh$_x$ observed a spin solid phase transition in the $x=0.65$ composition over a very narrow temperature range. To better understand this transition, we investigated how it affects the long-range order of the neutrons using polarized neutron reflectometry. Our findings indicate that the development of the spin solid phase causes significant depolarization of the neutrons, which increases as the temperature decreases. A model was used to analyze the results, which revealed that the spin correlations within the spin solid phase are very strong. Furthermore, the study shows that the presence of a ferromagnetic state at higher temperatures also contributes to the depolarization of the neutrons. A comparison with previous studies of CeFe$_{1-x}$Co$_x$ revealed some similarities, but the overall depolarization was found to be less pronounced in CePd$_{1-x}$Rh$_x$.

A unique feature of some high-mass star-forming regions is the presence of narrow-line self-absorption in their HI spectra, indicating the absorption of background radiation by dense gas near the region's surface. Two narrow-line self-absorption components were identified in the direction of G176.51+00.20 using HI spectra from the GALFA-HI survey at frequencies of 4.55 and 5.04 km/s, specifically in the form of inverted T$_B$ profiles. These self-absorption components correspond to dense gas with column densities of approximately 1.95 and 1.65 $\times$ 10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$ and temperatures of 35 and 50 K, respectively. Their location can be inferred from the positions of their critical densities and the velocities of their peak emission, placing them at a distance of around 5.5 kpc from Earth and 1-2 pc from the region's central stars, where high-density gas is actively accumulating to form high-mass stars.

We introduce a new class of dynamical systems, called avaricious $\beta$-shifts with a gap, as a subset of $\beta$-shifts. These systems have a gap in their transfer function, indicating no orbits of finite length can land on more than one element at once. By demonstrating that all intermediate $\beta$-shifts fall within this category, we prove they are topologically mixing only when the transfer function has a gap large enough to meet specific conditions. Furthermore, we show that when $\beta$ is an algebraic number, the size of the gap can be determined from its irreducible polynomial.

The value of the CP angle phi s has been determined from data collected by the LHCb detector in proton-proton collisions at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies, resulting in 3.0 fb-1 of integrated luminosity. Decays of Bs mesons into J/\psi pi+pi- pairs were analyzed, and phi s was found to be -0.019 +/- 0.17 +/- 0.02 radians, consistent with the Standard Model's expected value.

Deep neural networks are widely used in various image recognition tasks, with numerous research papers and implementations available online. However, deep neural networks are often tailored to a specific image dataset and may not perform well in other applications. As a result, there is a growing need for effective methods to adapt pre-trained neural networks to new image recognition tasks. This study assesses the performance of several deep neural network domain transfer methods on the CIFAR-10 dataset, with a focus on identifying the strengths, limitations, and recommendations for each approach.

Consider the projective plane $\mathbb P_{q+1}(\mathbb F_q)$ where $q$ is a power of $p$, and $1 \leq a < b < \infty$ with $a+b = \min\{2q-2, 2q-1\}$. The number of $(2, p, k)$ arcs in $\mathbb P_{q+1}(\mathbb F_q)$ for $k \leq a+q-1$ and $k \leq b+q-1$ is determined through a direct count, leading to an exact formula for $k > 2$. Specifically, for $k = p^m$, the count reveals a formula in terms of $m$, and more surprisingly, for fixed $m$, as $p$ varies in powers of $q$, a formula in terms of the binomial coefficient and Legendre symbol. Notably, for $k = p^m$ and $m \geq 2$, the count reveals a decreasing trend with increasing $m$, and in the case of a singular arc with $|k| \leq 2$, the count reveals a formula in terms of the quadratic residue character and Legendre symbol.

In a regular triangular lattice, the relationship between a central triangle and four surrounding triangles has a connection to counting steps in a path on a triangular board, and also relates to a lattice triangle's area. This "proof without words" uses visual demonstration and an additional verbal explanation to establish the connection.

Graph Neural Networks are now a leading choice for handling intricate graph data, offering improved accuracy compared to conventional machine learning methods. Despite their success, creating training datasets that can keep up with the growing demand for accurate models has become increasingly difficult. To address this challenge, we propose a unique framework that allows for the systematic modification of GNN models to achieve state-of-the-art performance on specific graph challenges. Our approach, built on a parameterized interpreter, evaluates how adjustments to key parameters (like filter size or depth) impact the model's performance across various graph tasks through an in-depth analysis of (i) the model's adaptability to different graph characteristics, (ii) the model's feature learning dynamics. This method has been successfully tested on three prominent graph challenges, demonstrating a clear connection between parameterized settings and task-specific performance. Furthermore, we discovered that GNNs with comparable architecture exhibit task-specific variability to a notable extent, and that certain parameterized settings are common across multiple graph tasks.

We analyzed X-ray data from the Chandra observatory to investigate the galaxy cluster RXCJ0232.2-4420. This analysis allowed us to create detailed 0.5-7 keV surface brightness images and a temperature map with an approximate error of 20%. Our findings indicate that the galaxy cluster RXCJ0232.2-4420 exhibits complex structures on multiple scales. In the southern region, we discovered a significant substructure separated from the main cluster by a 1.5 sigma confidence interval boundary. However, we were unable to confirm any notable subhalos within this substructure. On a larger scale, we detected a 4 sigma confidence interval cold front in the northern part of the cluster. Our temperature measurements in this cluster reveal a north-south temperature gradient of approximately 0.6 keV. This temperature discrepancy cannot be fully explained by gravitational processes alone, suggesting that Maccaccaro's afterglow may be responsible for the observed X-ray emission.

Originally developed for language models, the Legendre Memory Module has shown potential in training neural networks in a parallel manner, making it suitable for tasks requiring rapid inference and high throughput. This paper demonstrates successful parallel training of the Legendre Memory Module for convolutional and recurrent neural networks. It highlights specific strategies and data augmentation techniques that can be employed to maintain consistency in the input distribution among multiple networks. Furthermore, the paper presents different approaches to initializing multiple networks and compares various methods to facilitate training in parallel. It also validates the effectiveness of the proposed techniques on a range of real-world applications, including image classification (ResNet, MobileNet, and VGG models) and language classification (IMDB and Stanford Sentiment Dataset).

As we progress through summer, a fresh wave of cosmic rays brings new life to particle physics, offering a way to look for elusive particles that have evaded detection.  I'll provide an update on the status of weakly-interacting particles such as WIMPs, followed by a review of alternative targets, including sterile neutrinos and axions, with a focus on the latter's potential across radio, glasma, x-ray, keV-cosmology, and optical/gamma-ray frontiers.  Furthermore, these efforts will be accompanied by innovative methods and a deeper understanding of the universe, with a focus on the latter's evolution.

We examine a complex network system where interchangeable agent avatars interact with their environment. These agents can move between locations on the network to better understand their surroundings. They also acquire and share information with other agents to gain a deeper understanding. In this system, exchange of information leads to linguistic and cultural diversity, resulting in inconsistent language usage. However, when existing knowledge is utilized to learn about their environment, multiple solutions emerge as the most effective method for survival. In this system, the naming information is used to identify environmental characteristics, and this information can be utilized to develop consistency in naming practices. In this study, the naming game is solved by identifying a consistent naming convention that provides the highest utility for all agents. In this system, local game dynamics and agent migration contribute to reaching an agreement on a consistent naming practice. In this study, the time it takes to reach an agreement is analyzed and this time is influenced by agent migration rate, density of exchange information, and degree distribution of the network.
